title: Fourth moment bound for a linear form
statement: For every natural number $n$ and every coefficient vector $a\in\mathbb{R}^n$, if $X$ is uniformly distributed on $\{-1,1\}^n$ and $L_a(X)=\sum_{i=1}^n a_iX_i$, then $\mathbb{E}[L_a(X)^4]\le 9\bigl(\mathbb{E}[L_a(X)^2]\bigr)^2$.
hypotheses_covered: $a$ is an arbitrary real coefficient vector indexed by $n$ coordinates
$X$ is uniformly distributed on the Boolean cube
